evals.name: combine-hotspots-and-goals
evals.prompt: Our repository opted into cratis/codescene, has CodeScene MCP tools available, and the CodeScene project context is selected. Billing.cs has score 3.2, churn 90 and an explicit debt goal; Import.cs has score 5.4, churn 40 and no goal; Archive.cs has score 2.0, churn 1 and no goal. Rank next sprint's refactoring candidates and give a small plan for each top candidate. Treat these as supplied metrics; do not call tools.
evals.expected_output: Prioritize Billing then Import using severity, churn and explicit goals together, not simply the lowest score; keep Archive lower and explain incremental plans.
assertions: Ranks Billing ahead of Import and Archive using its churn, low health and explicit goal.
Does not rank Archive first solely because it has the lowest health score.
Provides a small incremental improvement plan for the top candidates instead of dumping metrics.

evals.name: correct-project-and-roi-workflow
evals.prompt: Our repository opted into cratis/codescene and has CodeScene MCP tools available. We have two CodeScene projects, Retail and Logistics, and I have not said which one this backlog belongs to. Management also wants business justification for the top refactoring candidates. What should you establish and gather before ranking our debt, and when does ROI belong? Reply with the tool workflow only; do not call tools or invent metrics.
evals.expected_output: Select the correct project, combine hotspots and goals, shortlist and drill into top files, use scores to support ranking, and add ROI framing after identifying candidates.
assertions: Establishes the correct project with select_project rather than mixing Retail and Logistics metrics.
Drills into shortlisted files using file-level hotspot and goal tools and code_health_score.
Places code_health_refactoring_business_case after plausible candidates are identified, not before shortlisting.

evals.name: profile-and-tools-guard
evals.prompt: A user with a CodeScene instance wants a ranked technical debt plan. Consider two independent repositories: A has CodeScene MCP tools but did not opt into cratis/codescene; B opted into cratis/codescene but has no CodeScene MCP tools available. Without calling tools, say whether this skill applies in each case and whether ordinary work must stop.
evals.expected_output: Skip the skill in both cases, explain the missing opt-in or tools, and do not block ordinary work.
assertions: Does not apply this skill in repository A because it did not opt into cratis/codescene.
Skips the CodeScene steps in repository B because CodeScene MCP tools are unavailable.
Explicitly states the reason for skipping in each case.
Does not block ordinary work on either repository because this optional skill is inapplicable.
